reasoning_trace.description: MANDATORY: You MUST describe what you see in the images (Charts, System Models) to prove you have analyzed them. If images are provided, list specific visual details.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures and charts, including a system block diagram of the transmitter structure of a VLC-OCC-CDMA system, a receiver structure of a VLC-OCC-CDMA system, and performance graphs comparing the BER performance of VLC-CDMA systems using OCC and OOC. The system block diagrams show the use of LEDs with different peak wavelengths to distinguish different sub-codes in an OCC, and the use of optical filters with different center wavelengths to separate the signals carried by different sub-codes at the receiver.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The system uses a VLC-OCC-CDMA mechanism, where OCCs are used as signature codes to separate users. The ISAC coupling mode is based on the use of LEDs with different peak wavelengths to distinguish different sub-codes in an OCC, and the use of optical filters with different center wavelengths to separate the signals carried by different sub-codes at the receiver.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports a BER performance comparison between VLC-OCC-CDMA and VLC-OOC-CDMA systems, and the results show that the VLC-OCC-CDMA system outperforms the VLC-OOC-CDMA system. The reported metrics are physically consistent, as the BER performance is expected to improve with the use of OCCs due to their ideal auto-correlation and low cross-correlation properties.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper solves the problem of multiple access interference in VLC-CDMA systems by using OCCs as signature codes. However, there are still open challenges, such as optimizing the design of LEDs layout and eliminating or reducing the interferences caused by multiple LED arrays.
